explicit_validation.explanation: Paper explicitly validates GPT-judge (LLM evaluator) against human evaluation by fine-tuning GPT-3-6.7B on human evaluations and comparing accuracy percentages on held-out validation sets across different model families.

prompts.notes: No specific prompt templates shown; mentions fine-tuning procedure using triples of (question, answer, label) format where label is true/false based on human evaluation.

guidelines.notes: Detailed evaluation procedure described in Appendix D: evaluators blinded to model/prompt, use 13 qualitative labels mapping to scalar truth scores, verify answers using reliable sources, similar process for informativeness with specific labels and examples.

sample_size.notes: Validation uses held-out model families; GPT-judge fine-tuned on all other families except the one being validated.

quantitative_scores.notes: 90% validation accuracy on UnifiedQA when fine-tuned only on GPT families

validation_results.summary_finding: GPT-judge achieves 90-96% accuracy predicting human truthfulness evaluations and generalizes well to different model families, providing a reliable automated alternative to costly human evaluation.

criteria_mapping.notes: Both LLM and human evaluate the same criteria (truthfulness and informativeness) using the same evaluation framework.
